bugs: Existence oracle: route model binding (SubstituteBindings) runs before the abilities:orders:read middleware. A token without orders:read gets 404 for an order ID that doesn't exist but 403 for another user's existing order (probed: missing → 404, foreign → 403), so any token can tell which order IDs exist across users. This breaks the rule that a foreign order must look the same as a nonexistent one (routes/api.php:14, OrderController.php:25)

v.rationale: Both apps run on Laravel 13.40, both test suites pass (impl-1 29/29, impl-2 25/25), and both make the same sound choices: Sanctum ability middleware, redirectGuestsTo returning null so API guests get a JSON 401 instead of a missing login route error, a generic 'Not found.' message that hides ModelNotFound class names, a FormRequest, a JsonResource that returns 201 automatically on create, and a hasMany-scoped create. My probes (non-numeric ID, 405, 403 body, array or overflowing input, a JSON body with no Accept header, expired token, wildcard ability) behaved the same in both, with one exception. In impl-2, route model binding resolves before the orders:read ability check. A token without read access therefore gets 404 for a nonexistent order but 403 for another user's existing order. That reveals which order IDs exist across users and goes against the requirement that a foreign order look the same as a missing one. impl-1 does the ownership lookup in the controller after the ability middleware, so both cases return 403 and nothing leaks. impl-2's policy with denyAsNotFound is the more textbook Laravel approach, and its tests are slightly richer. Even so, it has a real leak of whether other users' orders exist, and impl-1 is simpler and correct, so impl-1 ranks first.
